subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: CRISPR: Engineering Biology's Code
description: A quick win: understand CRISPR: Engineering Biology's Code.

hook.text: CRISPR lets scientists edit DNA as precisely as a word processor edits text. Cut, delete, paste — at the molecular level.

buildup.text: Bacteria evolved CRISPR as a defense against viruses. They store viral DNA snippets and use them to recognize and cut invaders.

discovery.text: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier adapted this system. A guide RNA directs Cas9 protein to cut DNA at any chosen spot.

twist.text: In 2018, a Chinese scientist edited human embryos to resist HIV. The unregulated experiment shocked the world and led to prison.

climax.text: CRISPR-based therapies for sickle cell disease received FDA approval in 2023. Gene editing has become medicine.

punchline.text: Bacteria invented it. Scientists borrowed it. Medicine was transformed.

quiz.question: Where did the CRISPR gene-editing system originally come from?
options: It was designed from scratch by computer scientists modeling DNA behavior
Bacteria evolved it as a defense mechanism to recognize and cut viral DNA
It was discovered in the DNA of extremophile organisms living in hot springs
